t: This was King's Theatre, a live entertainment venue on the corner of Hammersmith Road and Rowan Road. It is no longer a theatre. It was built in 1902 as a music hall, with room for three thousand people. The architect was W. G. R. Sprague, who trained under Frank Matcham and then set up his own practice. He designed at least thirty-five theatres between 1890 and 1929, so this big music hall was one of many from a very prolific hand.
